newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST -- Czech Republic -- Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST -- Czech Republic -- Jan 15.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Finance Ministry's proposal to increase value added tax on electricity and gas from five percent to 22 percent beginning this July is agitating energy companies. The companies believe that if the proposal is accepted, the cabinet will not have the courage to begin fast reforms of energy pricing for households.
- The government plans to create at least partial cushions for public debts, whose fast increase the Finance Ministry has in the past few years only monitored.
- Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy announced that inflation and the increasing foreign trade deficit are the biggest problems in the Czech economy.

PRAVO - Four out of 58 members of the Social Democratic Party (CSSD), Pavel Dostal, Zdenek Jicinsky, Jaromir Schling and Frantisek Spanbauer, will definitely support the Czech-German Declaration during the vote in parliament, while 27 CSSD members have stated than they will under no circumstances vote in favor of the declaration.
- The government budget for 1996, after years of well-balanced and even surplus economics, will finish with a deficit amounting to approximately two billion crowns.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Member of parliament Ondrej Zemin, who is one of the five representatives discovered to be falsely using their titles (JUDr for Zemin), announced yesterday that he will resign from his post. His party member Tomas Kladivko will take his place.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - While this year citizens are expecting a one third increase in electricity and gas prices, experts say that another similar price increase can be expected next year.

- After a delay of many weeks, Chairman of Parliament Milos Zeman presented President Havel with a fifty page document, for which the head of the Social Democratic Party (Zeman) wants his confirmation that a group of people from the Interior Ministry and secret services were illegally observed by politicians.
